messages:
Maya: heads-up — did a quick bring-up for the new 'tide-iso' embedding candidate with two quant configs (per-tensor int8, per-channel int8) and noticed weird recall divergence for very short queries (1-3 tokens).

Liam: can you paste the run command + quick metrics?

Maya: sure. ran the usual holdout suite (wiki+qa shorttail) with normalization on/off. command:```./run_eval --model tide-iso --embed-dim 1024 --quant per-channel --norm l2 --queries shorttail --k 5```

Maya: per-channel int8, norm=l2 -> recall@1 0.62, recall@5 0.85, silhouette 0.21, umap looks ok but tiny clusters for 1-token queries.

Maya: per-tensor int8, norm=l2 -> recall@1 0.55, recall@5 0.78, silhouette 0.16, much more cluster overlap on UM A P (screenshot posted in thread). :thinking_face:

Sarah: interesting. did you compare to fp16 baseline?

Maya: fp16 baseline (no quant) norm=l2 -> recall@1 0.64, recall@5 0.86, silhouette 0.23. so per-channel nearly matches fp16 except for the 1-token tail, per-tensor loses more.

Dinesh: what about norm off? sometimes norm interacts badly with short tokens if tokenization produces weird freq patterns.

Maya: turned norm off intentionally for a pass. results: per-channel int8 norm=none -> recall@1 0.47, recall@5 0.72. fp16 norm=none -> recall@1 0.49, recall@5 0.74. so normalization recovers most of the loss for short queries, but per-tensor still behind.

Liam: so hypothesis: quantization + lack of l2 norm exacerbates angular distortion for short vectors (low-context queries). per-channel quant reduces distortion. can we run PCA or cosine drift delta between fp16 and quant vectors?

Maya: ran delta-cosine script on 10k short queries. median cosine(fp16, per-channel) = 0.985, median cosine(fp16, per-tensor) = 0.948. distribution shows heavier tail under 0.8 for per-tensor. pasted mini histogram.

Sarah: that matches recall drop. Might also be a scale calibration issue: per-tensor scales a single factor that hurts rare-token embeddings. Could try per-channel + clip or per-channel + small bias recenter.

Dinesh: another lever: run GPTQ-style per-channel fine-tune (calib on small corpus) — we saw improvements on other models. Can you add a 512-sample calibration set?

Maya: queued a run:```./quant_calibrate --model tide-iso --method gptq --calib-samples 512 --out tide-iso-gptq.pc``` Will report when done. ETA ~30m.

Eval-Bot: job 884412 queued on cluster-3. will post results to thread.

Maya: quick note — UMAP for short queries shows a striping artifact when norm=none + per-tensor. suspect zero-centering mismatch. ran mean-centering on embeddings before umap and striping reduced.

Liam: good catch. can you attach the snippet you used for mean-centering?

Maya: snippet:```python
# center before umap
X = X - X.mean(axis=0, keepdims=True)
X = X / (np.linalg.norm(X, axis=1, keepdims=True) + 1e-12)  # optional l2
```

Sarah: do we have a production concern? i.e., if customers use short queries (search box etc.) will they see regressions on per-tensor quant models?

Dinesh: yes — for PLG customers with short prompts, per-tensor could be regressive. default quant profile should prefer per-channel or require norm. Might be a doc+console flag too.

Maya: action items: 1) finish GPTQ calib run, 2) compare per-channel+clip and per-channel+recenter, 3) run recall split by query length (1,2,3,4+ tokens) and produce shorttable. I'll post numbers and recommended default.

Liam: add an A/B test suggestion: deploy per-channel behind a canary route for 24h and measure short-query CTR. quick smoke:```@eval-bot run-canary --model tide-iso-gptq.pc --route /embeds/canary --duration 24h```

Eval-Bot: canary scheduled: route /embeds/canary -> tide-iso-gptq.pc, start: 4387660800, end: 4387747200. metrics will be fed to /dash/embeds/canary.

Maya: thanks all. will post follow-ups. if GPTQ doesn't help, recommend we pick per-channel quant + forced l2 normalization as the default jar for tide-iso. :white_check_mark:
